newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai finmin urges successor to watch tax revenue.
newsitem.headline: Thai finmin urges successor to watch tax revenue.

text.p: Thai Finance Minister Bodi Chunnananda on Wednesday urged his successor to monitor a declining trend of government tax revenue which he said may prevent Thailand from achieving its revenue target next year.

Bodi, expecting to be replaced after outgoing Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa steps down later this week, said government tax revenue has missed its target in the past three to four months and the trend may continue in the 1996/97 fiscal year starting October 1.

Bodi said a new Thai government may need to review the planned 984 billion baht ($39.4 billion) national expenditure in the deficit-free, balanced budget for the next fiscal year that was passed by parliament last month.
"The new finance minister should consider trimming planned expenditures...on the revenue side, tax collection should be streamlined to boost its efficiency," he said.
Bodi said the next government should not overspend its budget to avoid widening Thailand's current account deficit.
He recommended greater government efforts to trim spendings of state enterprises which have a combined annual investment that is bigger than the national budget.
